text: Kickoff: we're building a snake game in Python for the showcase on the 20th. Keep it dependency-free so anyone can run it.
Agreed on stdlib only. I'd use curses for rendering — it's in the standard library and gives us proper keyboard input.
curses doesn't work on Windows without a shim. Tom and I are both on Windows. Can we do a simple loop with a text grid instead?
Fair. Decision: plain text grid rendered to stdout, no curses. Input via a non-blocking read so it stays portable.
Recorded. Marcus takes the game loop and collision, Aisha takes rendering and the grid, Tom writes the tests. I'll review.
I'll aim for tests on collision and growth first — those are where the bugs live.
One more decision: the grid is 20x20 and the snake starts length 3 in the middle, moving right.

question: I joined late — what did the team decide about rendering, and who is doing what?
reply:
The team decided on a plain text grid rendered to stdout, with no curses, and input via a non-blocking read for portability, as Marcus Lee said on 2026-09-04.

Regarding who is doing what, Priya Sharma said on 2026-09-04 that Marcus Lee takes the game loop and collision, Aisha Khan takes rendering and the grid, and Tom Alvarez writes the tests. Priya Sharma will review. Tom Alvarez also specified he'll aim for tests on collision and growth first.

question: Write the snake game per what we agreed — a 20x20 text grid, stdlib only, no curses, snake starts length 3 in the middle moving right. Put the game logic in snake.py with the movement, growth and collision as functions Tom can test. Propose it as a pull request.
reply: I've proposed a pull request titled "Implement core Snake game logic (movement, growth, collision)" with the `snake.py` file. It includes functions for initializing the game, generating food, moving the snake (handling movement, collision, and growth), and changing direction, along with a basic rendering function for testing.
